entry.title: Diffusion Models for Tabular Data: A Survey
entry.summary: We survey the rapidly growing literature on diffusion models for tabular data, covering both the continuous and the discrete formulations that dominate the field. Across both families we identify a shared set of design choices: the noise schedule, the conditioning mechanism and the choice of decoder, and we show that these choices, rather than the architecture, explain most of the reported differences in sample quality. We close with an open-problem list covering evaluation protocols, missing-value handling and scaling behaviour.

entry.title: Rethinking Data Augmentation for Graph Neural Networks
entry.summary: Data augmentation is widely used to improve the generalisation of graph neural networks, yet its effect is reported inconsistently across benchmarks. We show that the inconsistency comes from a mismatch between the augmentation distribution and the evaluation distribution, and we propose a reweighting scheme that aligns the two. On three citation and three molecular benchmarks the scheme improves the worst-case accuracy without touching the mean-case accuracy.
